72974-recollections-of-james-anthony-gar.title: Recollections Of James Anthony Gardner Commander R N 1775 18
72974-recollections-of-james-anthony-gar.creator: Unknown
72974-recollections-of-james-anthony-gar.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. I know nothing of grammar;  At school they never could hammer  Or beat it into my head. The bare word made me stammer,  And turn pale as if I were dead. And here I may as well be telling  I’m often damned out in my spelling. And this is all the apology  I offer for my chronology,  And biographical sketches  Of mighty men, and lubberly wretches,  From seventeen hundred and seventy-seven—  Their rank, their titles, and their names are given.

arxiv-2205-10623.creator: M. Yu. Piotrovich*, S. D. Buliga, T. M. Natsvlishvili, M.Yu. Piotrovich, S.D. Buliga, T.M. Natsvlishvili
arxiv-2205-10623.description: Abstract We estimated the radiative efficiency and spin value for a number of local active galactic nuclei with z < 0.34 z<0.34 using 3 popular models connecting the radiative efficiency with such parameters of AGNs as mass of supermassive black hole, angle between the line of sight and the axis of the accretion disk and bolometric luminosity.

arxiv-2306-05348.title: Athermal quasistatic cavitation in amorphous solids: effect of random pinning
arxiv-2306-05348.creator: Umang A. Dattani, Smarajit Karmakar, Pinaki Chaudhuri
arxiv-2306-05348.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Umang A. Dattani, Smarajit Karmakar, Pinaki Chaudhuri. Amorphous solids are known to fail catastrophically via fracture, wherein cavitation at nano-metric scales is known to play a significant role. Micro-alloying via inclusions is often used as a means to increase the fracture toughness of amorphous solids. Modeling such inclusions as randomly pinned particles that move only affinely and do not participate in plastic relaxation, we study how the pinning influences the process of cavitation-driven fracture in an amorphous solid.

arxiv-2410-13716.title: Mirage - Bench : Automatic Multilingual Benchmark Arena for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
arxiv-2410-13716.creator: Nandan Thakur, Suleman Kazi, Ge Luo, Jimmy Lin, Amin Ahmad
arxiv-2410-13716.description: Abstract Traditional retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) benchmarks evaluate systems using heuristic-based metrics, but these require human preferences as the ground truth for reference. In contrast, arena-based benchmarks, where systems compete against each other, require an expensive large language model (LLM) as a judge for a reliable evaluation. We present a simple efficient technique to combine the best of both worlds.

pmc-11359098.title: Traditional Processing Can Enhance the Medicinal Effects of Polygonatum cyrtonema by Inducing Significant Chemical Changes in the Functional Components in Its Rhizomes
pmc-11359098.creator: Jianjun Shen, Weiting Pu, Qiyan Song, Bihuan Ye, Xiaoxiao Shi, Youwu Chen, Yefei Yu, Haibo Li, Gary J Stephens
pmc-11359098.description: The aims of this study were to explore the significant chemical changes in functional components induced by the traditional processing method and evaluate whether this method based on nine cycles of steaming and drying can effectively enhance the medicinal effects of Polygonatum cyrtonema rhizome.

pmc-13225669.title: Regularized regression in ultra-small chemometric datasets: A methodological case study using FTIR spectra of Schiff bases
pmc-13225669.creator: Khudhayr Abdullah Rashedi, Tariq Saleh Alshammari, Khalid Mohammed Alshammari, Talal Abdulrahman Alanazi, Javid Shabbir, Tahir Mehmood
pmc-13225669.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study is not intended to establish a predictive framework for reaction yield. Instead, it is framed as a methodological investigation examining the statistical behavior and instability of regularized regression techniques when applied to ultra-small, high-dimensional chemometric datasets. The analysis is based on a curated dataset of Schiff base compounds (n = 21) for which post-synthesis Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectra and experimentally reported reaction yields are available. Structural information for all compounds is fully disclosed to ensure chemical transparency.

pmc-13347796.title: Health inequalities in infectious disease modelling
pmc-13347796.creator: Rosalind M. Eggo, Alexis Robert, Kamlesh Khunti, Hannah E. Clapham
pmc-13347796.description: Infectious disease transmission is unequal, with some groups experiencing long-standing higher burdens of infection and disease. Here, we discuss the urgent need for the field of transmission modelling to develop methods, collaborations and understanding of the drivers and dynamics of infectious disease inequalities to support policymaking that aims to mitigate inequalities.

pmc-13380577.title: Toward reliable thalamic segmentation: an evaluation of automated methods for structural MRI
pmc-13380577.creator: Georgios P. D. Argyropoulos, Christopher R. Butler, Manojkumar Saranathan
pmc-13380577.description: Automated thalamic nuclear segmentation has contributed towards a shift in neuroimaging analyses, from treating the thalamus as a homogeneous, passive relay, to a set of individual nuclei, embedded within distinct brain-wide circuits. However, many studies continue to widely rely on FreeSurfer’s segmentation of T1-weighted structural MRIs, despite their poor intrathalamic nuclear contrast.

pmc-13563688.title: Classification of Adolescent Drinking via Behavioral, Biological and Environmental Variables: A Machine Learning Approach With Bias Control
pmc-13563688.creator: Ruobing Liu, Mohamed Azzam, Nicole L. Zabik, Shibiao Wan, Jennifer Urbano Blackford, Jieqiong Wang
pmc-13563688.description: In 2024, approximately 30% of US adolescents reported having consumed alcohol at least once in their lifetime, with about 25% of these individuals engaging in binge drinking. Adolescent alcohol use is associated with neurodevelopmental impairments, elevated risk of later alcohol use and mental health disorders.

pmc-13580184.title: Synthesis, Characterization and Reactivity of Alkyl Iron(II) PCP Pincer Complexes
pmc-13580184.creator: Matthias Käfer, Simon Gstöttner, Berthold Stöger, Antoine Dupé, Luis F. Veiros, Karl Kirchner
pmc-13580184.description: The syntheses and reactivity of a series of alkyl iron PCP pincer complexes is described. The alkyl complexes of the type [Fe­(PCPCH2-iPr)­(R)­(CO)2] (R = CH3, CH2CH3, CH2CH2CH3, CH2CH2CH2CH3) are accessible in good yields (69–78%) by reduction of [Fe­(PCPCH2-iPr)­(Br)­(CO)2] with sodium followed by oxidative addition of alkyl halides RX (X = Br or I).

pmc-13624491.title: Correlation between Prenatal Fetal Hemodynamic Parameters and Growth Indices in Pregnant Women with Preeclampsia and Neonatal Ultrasound Indicators of Organ Development
pmc-13624491.creator: Shudan Yin, Jianhong Wang, Jinying Liu
pmc-13624491.description: Objectives:This retrospective study aimed to explore the associations between prenatal fetal hemodynamics and growth parameters in pregnant women with preeclampsia and neonatal ultrasound assessment indicators of organ development.Methodology:Clinical parameters of 296 pregnant women and their neonates admitted to Xi’an Fourth Hospital from December 2024 to December 2025 were collected.

pmc-13634685.title: Infectious complications of dental procedures in dogs and cats, and the impact of antimicrobial prophylaxis: a systematic review
pmc-13634685.creator: J. S. Weese, M. Soltero‐Rivera, H. E. Weese, K. Scahill
pmc-13634685.description: ObjectivesTo identify and describe available evidence pertaining to the local and systemic infectious complications in dogs and cats that have undergone dental procedures and the impact of peri‐procedural antimicrobial prophylaxis.Materials and MethodsA systematic review was performed based on Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and MetaAnalysis guidelines.

pmc-13646352.title: Quality of Diabetes Care Among Older Adults in Germany—Results of the Study on Health of Older People 2022/2023 Compared With Previous National Health Surveys
pmc-13646352.creator: Yong Du, Giselle Sarganas, Beate Gaertner, Maike Buchmann, Judith Fuchs, Hannelore Neuhauser, Christin Heidemann
pmc-13646352.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimsThe study aims (1) to evaluate the quality of diabetes care considering guideline‐recommended medical therapies, cardiometabolic factors, and self‐management of health behaviours among older adults with diabetes in Germany, and (2) to examine time trends.Materials and MethodsPeople aged 66 years and older with diabetes were identified from the examination part of the German national Study on Health of Older People (Gesundheit65+) in 2022/2023.
